reasoning_traces.think:
Kairosis models forecast evolution as a sequence of independent Dirichlet-categorical distributions separated by a single unknown change point. The likelihood function splits forecasts into pre- and post-change segments, assigning each segment a Dirichlet prior with specific pseudo-counts α_k and α'_k. Pre-change pseudo-counts α_k = λ·t_CP reflect diversified historical influence, while post-change α'_k = 1 assumes concentrated agreement. The posterior is computed via Bayes’ rule, integrating over all possible change times r to yield a posterior mass function. This enables dynamic weighting of forecasts based on regime stability. The method fails under multiple change points due to combinatorial complexity and performs less well on continuous domains due to mismatched assumptions. In GSE, this translates to adaptive engine probability reweighting during live games, where sudden shifts in information (e.g., injury reports) trigger recalibration of belief weights.
